newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway C.Bank head sees '97 inflation near 2.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Norway C.Bank head sees '97 inflation near 2.5 pct.

text.p: Kjell Storvik, governor of Norway's central bank, said on Monday the bank would reduce its inflation forecast for 1997 to around 2.5 percent in its next quarterly forecast report in June.
In March, the bank estimated 1997 inflation at between 2.75 and 3.0 percent.

"I would indicate that we are coming a little bit further down to say around 2.5 percent for this year and maybe even a lower estimate for 1998," Storvik said in an interview with Reuters Financial Television (RFTV).
Storvik said this year's wage negotiations had been "much more favourable" than the bank had expected in its March report and at the same time electricity prices had fallen.
"So I think the future outlook for inflation is a little bit better and has improved since we presented our report in March," he said.
